ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 - ENGL 350 - Writing about Literature, Text, and Culture - Writing About Poetry - Gillen Wood - Poetry is a complex, playful art form acutely observant of human feeling and behavior, and marks the origins of what we call literature. In our first unit, we will read, recite, and analyze the verbal art of a suite of modern British and American poets, from Keats and Emily Dickinson to Langston Hughes and William Carlos Williams. This unit will also introduce students to foundational questions of poetics such as form, voice, and figurative language. A notable poetic tradition, inherited from nineteenth-century Romanticism, also looks outward, training its eye on the natural world around us. In our second unit, on recent American eco-poetry, we will examine how poetry is uniquely gifted to articulate human dependency on natural resources, and to map, psychologically, our apparently ungovernable impulses for consumption and environmental waste. Can so-called eco-poetry also help us imagine a resilient, post-carbon life mode and politics? Discussion of key concepts in ecology and the Anthropocene will supplement our readings in American ecopoetry from the mid-twentieth century to today.
